subsection: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
question_text: Dwight Eisenhower is famous for many things. Name one.

official_answers.text: President at the end of (during) the Korean War
Signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956 (Created the Interstate System)

why_it_matters.text: Eisenhower had two of America's biggest jobs in 12 years. As General, he commanded the D-Day invasion of Europe in 1944 — the largest amphibious war operation in history — that helped defeat Nazi Germany. Then as 34th president (1953-61), he ended the Korean War, built the Interstate Highway System, and warned Americans about the 'military-industrial complex.'

fun_fact.text: Eisenhower's Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956 created the U.S. Interstate Highway System — but its official name was the National Interstate and defense Highways Act. It was a national security project: highways to move troops fast in case of war. The 47,000-mile system Americans drive on every day is now named the Eisenhower Interstate System.
